package_info.package_versions: log4j: all versions; springframework: all except 3.1.8.RELEASE and 4.1.9.RELEASE
package_info.why_malicious: These policies are not about malware, but about enforcing architectural and security standards by banning risky or unapproved dependencies. The intent is to prevent the use of components (like log4j or unapproved springframework versions) that may introduce vulnerabilities or violate organizational standards.

execution_context.file_location: IQ Server policy configuration (No log4j policy)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the policy checks if any dependency matches the groupId 'org.apache.logging.log4j' and flags the build as failed if found.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is not malicious code, but a defensive policy to prevent the use of a risky or deprecated library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, developers might expect to use any dependency, but this policy enforces a ban on a specific family of components.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Banning known-vulnerable or deprecated libraries is a common security practice.
key_indicators: Wildcard match on groupId for log4j
Fail action on all build stages

execution_context.file_location: IQ Server policy configuration (Spring Framework Unapproved policy)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Coordinates match maven:org.springframework*:*:*:*
Coordinates do not match maven:org.springframework*:3.1.8.RELEASE:*
Coordinates do not match maven:org.springframework*:4.1.9.RELEASE:*
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the policy checks if any dependency is from the 'org.springframework' group, and if so, ensures it is either version 3.1.8.RELEASE or 4.1.9.RELEASE; any other version triggers a warning or failure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is not malicious code, but a strict version enforcement policy to ensure only approved, patched versions of a framework are used.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Developers may expect to use any version, but this policy enforces only the latest patch versions for security and stability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enforcing version pinning to avoid known vulnerabilities or bugs.
key_indicators: Explicit allow-listing of only two versions
Fail or warn actions on unapproved versions

attack_chain.action: Policy checks dependencies for banned or unapproved components during build or proxy resolution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Build fails or warnings are issued if policies are violated, preventing risky components from entering the codebase.

behavioral_signatures: Dependency resolution checks for banned groupIds or unapproved versions
Fail or warn actions triggered by policy violations
file_indicators: IQ Server policy configurations with wildcard or explicit version constraints
Build logs showing policy violation failures
network_indicators: N/A (no external network behavior, local policy enforcement)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build and proxy logs for policy violation messages related to banned groupIds (e.g., org.apache.logging.log4j) or unapproved versions (e.g., springframework not 3.1.8.RELEASE or 4.1.9.RELEASE). Review IQ Server policy configurations for wildcard bans or explicit allow-lists.
